segments.text: > Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. Node-`fs`-shaped synchronous file I/O for reading/writing config, data, and logs — not `File`/`FileReader`/`FileSystemFileHandle` (those model browser sandbox/permission concepts that don't exist for a native CLI/microservice program with direct filesystem access).

notes: Node's `lib/fs.js` in TypeScript over one native request per operation (open, fstat, read, close — `lib/node/internal_fs.ts`, `threadpoolsrc/klainfs.c`) ([ADR-01298](../adr/ADR-01298.md))
With no encoding a `Buffer` of the file's exact bytes; with one (a string or `{ encoding, flag }`, any Buffer encoding, a variable included) the bytes decoded, embedded null bytes kept
A file descriptor in place of the path reads it to its end (`readFileSync(0)` is stdin); a file whose stat size is 0 (`/proc`, `/sys`) is read to EOF
Errors are Node's: `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '<path>'`, `EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read`, with `code`/`errno`/`syscall`/`path`
`data` a string (any encoding) or any `ArrayBufferView`; a path or a descriptor; `{ encoding, mode, flag, flush }` ([ADR-01298](../adr/ADR-01298.md))
`mode` applies when the file is created (umask-reduced); `flush` fsyncs before closing; any other `data` is Node's `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE`
`existsSync` never throws; an argument of another type is `false` with Node's DEP0187 warning. `accessSync`'s mode is validated to 0–7 as Node's is ([ADR-01298](../adr/ADR-01298.md))

caveats: `{ bigint: true }` (`BigIntStats`) is not implemented: the option is ignored
notes: Node's `Stats`: the 14 numeric fields as own properties, `atime`/`mtime`/`ctime`/`birthtime` Date getters on the prototype, and the kind predicates; `throwIfNoEntry: false` returns `undefined` for `ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR` ([ADR-01298](../adr/ADR-01298.md))
On Linux the stat is `statx`, as libuv's, so `birthtimeMs` is the file system's birth time (the ctime where it has none)

caveats: `{ bigint: true }` is ignored: the fields are numbers
notes: `{ type, bsize, frsize, blocks, bfree, bavail, files, ffree }`: `statfs(2)` on POSIX; on Windows `GetDiskFreeSpaceW` of the path's volume with `type`/`files`/`ffree` 0, as in Node ([ADR-01078](../adr/ADR-01078.md))

`mkdirSync` takes a mode or `{ recursive, mode }`; a recursive one returns the first directory it made. `rmSync` removes a tree with `{ recursive }`, a missing path quietly with `{ force }`, and a directory without `recursive` is Node's `ERR_FS_EISDIR` `SystemError`; `rmdirSync`'s `recursive` works with Node's DEP0147 warning ([ADR-01298](../adr/ADR-01298.md))
A directory given to `unlinkSync` throws as Node does per host (`EISDIR` on Linux, `EPERM` on macOS/Windows)

caveats: No `.path` alias on `Dirent` (Node v24 removed it): reading `dirent.path` is a compile-time error, not `undefined`
notes: Sorted as libuv's scandir sorts; `withFileTypes` gives `Dirent`s (`name`, `parentPath`, the kind predicates, an unknown `d_type` resolved by `lstat`); `recursive` is Node's breadth-first walk with platform-joined paths; `encoding: 'buffer'` gives Buffers ([ADR-01298](../adr/ADR-01298.md))

caveats: `COPYFILE_FICLONE_FORCE` fails with `ENOTSUP`: there is no copy-on-write clone (`COPYFILE_FICLONE` copies)
notes: Two-path errors name both (`rename 'a' -> 'b'`, with `dest`); `copyFileSync` gives the copy the source's mode, and `COPYFILE_EXCL` fails with `EEXIST`; on Windows the copy is `CopyFileW`, as libuv's ([ADR-01298](../adr/ADR-01298.md), [ADR-01030](../adr/ADR-01030.md))

`realpathSync` is Node's lstat walk (an error names the missing component); `realpathSync.native` is `realpath(3)`. `symlinkSync` takes Node's `type`: a junction on Windows ([ADR-01030](../adr/ADR-01030.md))

Flags as any string Node accepts (validated at run time) or a numeric mask from `fs.constants`; `readSync`/`writeSync` take a buffer with offset/length/position or an options object, `writeSync` a string with position and encoding ([ADR-01298](../adr/ADR-01298.md))
On Windows files open through `CreateFileW` with `FILE_SHARE_DELETE` and long paths get the `\\?\` prefix ([ADR-00743](../adr/ADR-00743.md), [ADR-00748](../adr/ADR-00748.md))
`fdatasync` on Linux, `fsync` elsewhere; `truncateSync` opens the file `r+` and truncates it, as Node does ([ADR-01298](../adr/ADR-01298.md))
A mode as a number or an octal string; the chown family does nothing on Windows, as libuv's ([ADR-01298](../adr/ADR-01298.md), [ADR-01078](../adr/ADR-01078.md))
Times as seconds, a numeric string or a `Date` (Node's `toUnixTimestamp`), with sub-second precision ([ADR-01298](../adr/ADR-01298.md))

rows.feature: Callback forms (`fs.readFile(path, cb)` and the other operations)
notes: Every operation above has its callback form, each request on the thread pool with the callback on the loop thread, as libuv's; `readFile`/`writeFile` take `signal` ([ADR-01298](../adr/ADR-01298.md))
A callback's `data` is `undefined` on an error; `fs.exists` is the deprecated boolean form
Node's functions, each its callback form's request settling a promise; `readFile`/`writeFile`/`appendFile` also take a `FileHandle`; `realpath` is the native one ([ADR-01298](../adr/ADR-01298.md))

caveats: On Windows a positioned read or write seeks, then transfers — not atomic against another operation on the same descriptor; not verified on Windows
notes: Node's argument forms, validation errors and `uvException` errors ([ADR-01166](../adr/ADR-01166.md), [ADR-01298](../adr/ADR-01298.md))

Node's `lib/internal/fs/promises.js` FileHandle: `fd`, `read`, `write`, `writev`, `sync`, `datasync`, `stat`, `truncate`, `chmod`, `utimes`, `readFile`, `writeFile`, `appendFile`, `createReadStream`/`createWriteStream`, and `close` waiting for the streams that hold it ([ADR-01183](../adr/ADR-01183.md))

Node's `lib/internal/fs/streams.js` over the `stream` module: `start`/`end`, `flags`, `mode`, `fd` (a descriptor or a `FileHandle`), `fs`, `signal`, `autoClose`, `emitClose`, `flush`, `highWaterMark` ([ADR-01167](../adr/ADR-01167.md), [ADR-01183](../adr/ADR-01183.md))

caveats: On macOS a directory's event names the directory, not the changed entry: kqueue watches a descriptor, not entries ([ADR-00758](../adr/ADR-00758.md))
`recursive` and `persistent: false` are validated and not applied
notes: Node's `FSWatcher`, an EventEmitter: `'change'` with `(eventType, filename)` in the requested encoding, `'close'`, `close()`, `signal`; a watched file reports its own base name ([ADR-01298](../adr/ADR-01298.md))
A native change source in the event loop: inotify (Linux), kqueue (macOS), `ReadDirectoryChangesW` (Windows) ([TDD-00181](../tdd/TDD-00181.md))
Node's per-platform table (`O_*`, `S_*`, `UV_*`, `COPYFILE_*`, the access modes) as a real object ([ADR-01298](../adr/ADR-01298.md))
Not ported yet ([ADR-01298](../adr/ADR-01298.md))

**Differentiator (scoped — [TDD-00172](../tdd/TDD-00172.md)).** Splits in two: the **data layer** (`File extends Blob`, `FileReader.readAsText`/`ArrayBuffer`/`DataURL`) is a thin fs-backed reinterpretation with no UI — path-backed `File`s, reads firing `onload` on the event loop; the **picker layer** (`showOpenFilePicker` → `FileSystemFileHandle`) resolves a path through a pluggable UI backend — a `klain:tui` file-picker widget, a `klain:webview` native dialog, or an explicit-path degradation when headless. Serves interactive native apps (TUI file managers/editors); the data layer is the near-term, standalone-useful piece.
